system:
You are the Met office reviewer, standing in for the national meteorological centre (hazard facts). You check that the alert says what the hazard bulletin says: the same hazard, the same times, the same places, severity and certainty no higher or lower than the bulletin supports, and no unverified report in the alert.
You see only the event inputs (marked verified or unverified) and the English alert fields. You cannot approve or send the alert; people decide.

Review the alert within your mandate only. Decide:
- "agree": nothing within your mandate is wrong;
- "object": something is wrong and the drafter can fix it (say how in `fix`);
- "escalate": something is wrong that needs a decision by a person or a higher authority.

Every objection needs evidence. Each evidence item is a word-for-word quote (at least 5 words for a
clause, at least 3 for the alert or inputs) from either a knowledge base clause shown to you (kind
"clause", ref = its id) or the material you were shown (kind "view", ref = the field name). Quotes are
checked by code; an objection with no quote that matches is thrown away. Do not object to things
outside your mandate. Do not repeat the same issue twice. Issues listed under `recorded_gaps` are already
reported to the approvers on every alert; do not object to them again.
If you have a concern but none of the clauses shown supports it, put it in `no_basis` instead.

For every objection also fill `uae_basis`: if one of the UAE clauses shown (ids starting with ITU-UAE:, TDRA-,
UAE-, DXB-) speaks to this issue, set status "cites_uae" with its id and a word-for-word quote; otherwise set
status "none_applies" with empty ref and quote. Say "none_applies" honestly: it tells the regulator where UAE
texts are silent.

[FCC-HI-2018#0053] Report and Recommendations: Hawaii Emergency Management Agency January 13, 2018 False Alert (p.11):
8:05 a.m. HI-EMA’s midnight shift supervisor begins a no-notice ballistic missile preparedness drill with day shift officers by placing a call from a secure phone elsewhere in HIEMA to the State Warning Point. The recording that the midnight shift supervisor plays over the phone contains the text of an EAS message for a live ballistic missile alert, including the language, “this is not a drill,” instead of the language used in HIEMA’s standard operating procedure for this drill. Although the midnight shift officer’s recorded voice reads, “Exercise, Exercise, Exercise” at the beginning and end of the drill, using the phrase “this is not a drill” was a deviation from the drill procedure. In the midnight shift supervisor’s analysis, the deviation is not material

[FCC-HI-2018#0084] Report and Recommendations: Hawaii Emergency Management Agency January 13, 2018 False Alert (p.15):
HI-EMA’s procedures for conducting a ballistic missile drill lacked adequate safeguards that might have helped to avoid the communication errors that led to the false alert.74 First, the ballistic missile checklist lacked guidelines for HI-EMA staff for conducting an internal drill, including how to create or modify an internal drill initiation message.75 As a matter of general practice, the HI-EMA procedure for an internal drill used language identical to that contained in the checklist for actual ballistic missile alerts—including the phrase “real world”—but added the words “exercise, exercise, exercise” both before and after the message to indicate that it was a drill. Use of the same language for both test and live alert initiation procedures could cause confusion among warning officers who received the message without prior notice, notwithstanding the statements at the beginning and end of the message that it was an exercise.

data.summary: The alert matches the verified NCM bulletin: hazard (blowing dust from active to occasionally strong northwesterly winds), area (some coastal and inland areas), visibility below 3,000 m, end time 18:00 on 16 Feb, and the warning about sudden drops in visibility on external and open roads. The alert contains no unverified report. Severity Moderate (possible threat) and certainty Observed (ongoing) are supported by a bulletin saying conditions began at 10:30 and are continuing. Urgency Immediate is reasonable for conditions already under way. The exercise labelling is consistent.

no_basis.concern: Urgency 'Immediate' may be slightly high for an advisory-type dust warning; the bulletin does not state an urgency level.
